title: Country Fried Steak and Eggs Breakfast
subtitle: Pounded cube steak, pepper gravy, and eggs over mashed potatoes.
description: Adapted from classic Texas diner chicken-fried steak tradition for a firehall plate breakfast: cube steak pounded thin, breaded and fried crisp, smothered in black pepper gravy and served with eggs and buttery mashed potatoes.

ingredients.name: all-purpose flour
ingredients.notes: seasoned with salt, pepper, garlic powder

ingredients.name: Yukon gold potatoes
ingredients.notes: peeled, boiled, and mashed with butter

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Country Fried Steak and Eggs Breakfast in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Steak. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Prep and bread steaks
steps.instruction: Season cube steaks with salt and pepper. Dredge in seasoned flour, dip in buttermilk, then coat again in flour pressing firmly so breading adheres. Rest breaded steaks on a rack 10 minutes so coating sets. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts.

steps.title: Fry the steaks
steps.instruction: Heat 1/2 inch oil in a large skillet to 350°F. Fry steaks in batches 3–4 minutes per side until deeply golden and internal temperature reaches 145°F for medium. Hold on a rack in a 200°F oven. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Make pepper gravy
steps.instruction: Pour off all but 1/4 cup drippings. Whisk in flour over medium heat 2 minutes until blonde. Slowly whisk in warm milk, simmer until thick enough to coat a spoon, and finish with cracked black pepper. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Mash potatoes and fry eggs
steps.instruction: Boil potatoes until fork-tender, drain, and mash with butter, salt, and warm milk until smooth. Fry eggs in a clean skillet over medium heat until whites are set (165°F) and yolks are runny. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Plate and serve
steps.instruction: Mound mashed potatoes on each plate, top with a fried steak, ladle pepper gravy generously over the top, and crown with a sunny-side egg. Serve immediately while breading stays crisp. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

stationWorkflow: Bread all steaks before frying starts so the line does not stall between batches.
Keep mashed potatoes in a covered hotel pan on low with a splash of cream stirred in.
Fry eggs in a separate pan while gravy simmers—never cook eggs in gravy grease.
cleanupNotes: Strain fry oil once cooled and wipe splatter from stovetop before it caramelizes.
Deglaze the gravy pan with hot water while warm to lift flour roux from corners.
leftovers: Reheat steaks on a rack at 375°F for 8 minutes; add fresh gravy rather than microwaving breading.
Chop leftover steak into a breakfast burrito with gravy, potatoes, and hot sauce.
